text_blocks.snippet: High blood pressure (hypertension) usually causes no symptoms at all, which is why doctors call it a "silent killer".
You can learn more about the condition from the Mayo Clinic or read the detailed overview at the Cleveland Clinic.
The Silent Nature of High Blood Pressure

list.snippet: Most people with high blood pressure feel completely normal.
You cannot rely on how you feel to know if your blood pressure is high.
The only way to know your numbers is to get your blood pressure checked with a cuff.

text_blocks.snippet: Symptoms of a Dangerous Spike (Hypertensive Crisis)

When blood pressure rises to dangerously high levels (above 180/120 mmHg), it can cause a medical emergency. Seek emergency care immediately if high blood pressure is accompanied by: National Institutes of Health (NIH) | (.gov) +1

list.snippet: Shortness of breath or trouble breathing
Signs of a stroke (like slurred speech or weakness on one side of the body)

text_blocks.snippet: Some people report minor signs when their pressure is elevated, though these are not guaranteed indicators:

list.snippet: Getting winded easily during mild activity
